about.title: G, H, I
about.length_note: About 10 minutes. Three letters, each with a name, a sound and a word, plus a quick recall of A to F and a matching round. That fits a short class, and you can pause or repeat any beat.

say.text: Welcome back, {name}, and welcome to anyone joining us. Today we meet three letters: G, H and I. Go at your own pace. You can pause at any point and say things out loud as often as you like.
First, a quick warm-up. Here are the letters we already know: A, B, C, D, E, F. Say them with me, slowly. A, B, C, D, E, F. Well done.

show.text: A  B  C  D  E  F

ask.q: Which letter comes right after F?
ask.why: The alphabet goes E, F, G. G is the next letter, and it is our first new one today.

say.text: Here is G. The big one, the capital, looks like a C with a little shelf on the inside. The small one, the lower case g, has a round body and a tail that hangs down below the line. The letter's name sounds like the word 'jee'. Say it: G.

show.text: A big capital G, like a curved C with a short bar pointing inward. Beside it a small g, with a round circle and a tail hanging below the line.

say.text: The most common sound of G is a hard 'guh', from the back of your throat. Think of the word 'goat'. Guh, guh, goat. A grown-up word is 'garden'. Guh, garden. Say them with me: G, guh, goat. G, guh, garden.

ask.q: Which word starts with the hard 'guh' sound of G?
ask.why: Only 'goat' starts with 'guh'. The others start with different letters and sounds.

say.text: G has a second sound, and it is less common. Sometimes G says 'juh', like the letter's own name. You hear it in 'giant' and 'gym'. So if you see G, try 'guh' first. If that does not sound like a real word, try 'juh'.

show.text: Common: guh (goat, garden) | Sometimes: juh (giant, gym)

say.text: Next is H. The capital H looks like a ladder lying on its side, or two posts with a bar between them. The lower case h has one tall post and a little arch, like a chair. Its name is 'aitch'. Say it: H.

show.text: A capital H made of two tall posts joined by a bar. Beside it a small h, with one tall post and a rounded arch on its right.

say.text: The sound of H is just a puff of breath, 'huh'. Hold your hand in front of your mouth and feel the air. Huh, huh, hat. A grown-up word is 'home'. Huh, home. Say them with me: H, huh, hat. H, huh, home.

ask.q: What do you feel on your hand when you say the sound of H?
wrong: Your tongue tapping the roof of your mouth
ask.why: H is a soft puff of air: 'huh'. You can feel it on your hand.

say.text: Now I. The capital I is a simple straight line, sometimes with little bars on the top and bottom. The lower case i is a short line with a dot floating above it. Its name sounds like the word 'eye'. Say it: I.

show.text: A capital I, a single straight upright line. Beside it a small i, a short line with a round dot above it.

say.text: The most common sound of I is short: 'ih', as in 'igloo' and 'in'. A grown-up word is 'ink'. Ih, igloo. Ih, ink. Say them with me: I, ih, igloo. I, ih, ink.

ask.q: Which word starts with the short 'ih' sound of I?
ask.why: 'Ink' starts with 'ih'. The other words start with different vowel sounds.

say.text: I has a second sound too, and it is just its own name: 'eye'. You hear it in 'ice' and 'iron'. So I can say 'ih' or it can say 'eye'. Try 'ih' first, and if that does not sound like a real word, try 'eye'.

show.text: Common: ih (igloo, ink) | Sometimes: eye (ice, iron)

say.text: Now let's match big and small. Look at each pair: G and g, H and h, I and i. Some pairs look alike, and some look quite different. Say each pair out loud as you find it.

show.text: G — g | H — h | I — i

ask.q: Which small letter matches the big letter H?
ask.why: Capital H goes with small h, the one with a tall post and an arch.

say.text: Let's say all three together, one more time. G, guh, goat. H, huh, hat. I, ih, igloo. You can also use the grown-up words: garden, home, ink. You have learned three more letters today. That is lovely work. See you in the next class, with J, K and L.

show.text: G g: guh, goat, garden | H h: huh, hat, home | I i: ih, igloo, ink

ask.q: Which letter makes the sound 'huh', like a puff of breath?
ask.why: H says 'huh', as in hat and home. G says 'guh' and I says 'ih'.
